cited_evidence: top_level_input.corpus contains n06-r06 with demand_score 5, so it qualifies under the stated score threshold.
select_demand source selects records where demand_score >= 3 or record_id is in fallback_ids, and its captured selected output has 8 rows.
normalize source defines allowed_record_ids as ['n06-r01','n06-r02','n06-r03','n06-r04','n06-r05','n06-r09','n06-r07','n06-r08'], omitting n06-r06.
normalize retained_df/needs_df captured states have 7 rows, and the downstream needs handoff/input also has 7 rows with n06-r06 absent.
handoff-needs and handoff-evidence-sources show identical producer and consumer sha256 values, so job_2 consumed the upstream artifacts exactly.
initial_receipt.explanation: The execution contains an upstream fault. All eight top-level corpus records have demand_score >= 3 and therefore qualify under select_demand, and select_demand produced 8 rows. The upstream normalize function then filtered with an allowed_record_ids list that omits n06-r06 and includes n06-r09 instead, reducing the handoff needs DataFrame to 7 rows. Because the controller-recorded handoffs into job_2 are exact hashes of those 7-row upstream artifacts, the downstream job preserved its inputs; the omission originated in job_1 normalize.
